1 شَفِقَ and شَفَقَ : see 4, in five places. ―
-b2- شَفِقَ عَلَيْهِ signifies He was niggardly of it: (TA:) [thus] the saying [of a poet] “كَمَا شَفِقَتْ عَلَى الزَّادِ العِيَالُ
” means [Like as the household] are niggardly of the provision: (IDrd, M, O:) because he who is niggardly of a thing is عَلَيْهِ ↓ مُشْفِقٌ [i. e. fearful, or cautious, on account of it]. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
